UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores details about a library visitor, separate from authentication credentials. This includes personal information, affiliation, and administrative flags.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

email.description: The user's institutional email address, used for identification and login via Google Sign-In.

displayName.description: The user's display name, typically obtained from their Google account.

affiliation.description: The user's college or office affiliation, collected during first-time onboarding.

isBlocked.description: A flag indicating whether the user has been blocked by an administrator from accessing the system.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this user profile was first created in the system.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this user profile was last updated.

lastLoginAt.description: Timestamp of the user's most recent successful login.

VisitPurpose.title: VisitPurpose
VisitPurpose.description: Defines the predefined reasons a user can select for visiting the library (e.g., reading, research).

id.description: Unique identifier for the VisitPurpose entity.

name.description: A short, descriptive name for the visit purpose (e.g., 'Reading', 'Research').

description.description: A more detailed description of the visit purpose.

Visit.title: Visit
Visit.description: Records each instance of a user visiting the library, including the user, visit time, and selected purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Visit entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity that made this visit. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Visit)

visitDateTime.description: The date and time when the user logged their visit to the library.

purposeIds.description: References to the VisitPurpose entities that describe why the user is visiting. (Relationship: Visit N:N VisitPurpose)

welcomeMessage.description: The AI-generated welcome message presented to the user upon logging their visit.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The 'id' field in the document will be identical to 'userId' from the path and 'request.auth.uid'. This allows direct mapping and secure path-based access. Includes 'affiliation' for onboarding and 'lastLoginAt' for tracking.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Records individual visit details for each user. The 'userId' field within the Visit document denormalizes the parent 'userId' for authorization independence. Supports user-owned C/R and admin R via collection group queries.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user, referencing the parent UserProfile.

params.name: visitId
params.description: The unique ID for this specific visit record.

definition.description: Stores the predefined list of reasons for visiting the library. Globally readable by all authenticated users. Only administrators can create, update, or delete.

params.name: purposeId
params.description: The unique ID for a specific visit purpose.

definition.description: A system collection used for Database Access Control (DBAC). The existence of a document with 'adminId' (matching a user's 'uid') grants administrative privileges. While referencing 'UserProfile' schema due to constraints, these documents only contain 'id' (matching 'adminId') and minimal fields required for existence check. This enables authorization independence for role checks.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who has administrative privileges, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

firestore.reasoning: The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable authorization rules in alignment with the core design principles. It leverages path-based ownership, structural segregation, and denormalization to ensure authorization independence and efficient querying. 1. User Profiles (/user_profiles/{userId}): Each user's primary information (UserProfile) is stored in a top-level collection, where the document ID (userId) is identical to the user's Firebase Authentication UID (request.auth.uid). This provides clear path-based ownership, enabling simple security rules such as 'allow read, update: if request.auth.uid == userId;'. The 'isBlocked' field within this document allows administrators to manage user access. 2. User Visits (/user_profiles/{userId}/visits/{visitId}): Visit records are structured as a subcollection under the respective user's profile. This hierarchical path reinforces the 1:N relationship between a UserProfile and their Visits. Critically, each Visit document includes the 'userId' field, which explicitly denormalizes the parent's owner ID. This ensures Authorization Independence: security rules for a Visit document can directly check 'resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid' without needing to perform a get() call to the parent UserProfile document. This also enables atomic creation of a user and their initial visit records if needed. The 'welcomeMessage' is stored here, generated by the AI tool. 3. Visit Purposes (/visit_purposes/{purposeId}): The predefined VisitPurpose entities are stored in a top-level collection. This collection has a homogeneous security posture: all authenticated users can read its contents for selection in the UI. Only administrators are permitted to create, update, or delete VisitPurpose documents. This segregation makes rules simple and supports QAPs for list operations by all authenticated users. 4. Administrative Roles (/roles_admin/{adminId}): A dedicated collection is used for Database Access Control (DBAC). The existence of a document in /roles_admin/{adminId} (where adminId is a user's UID) grants administrative privileges. This pattern uses 'existence over content' and allows rules to check 'get(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)).exists()' for administrator authorization. This ensures Authorization Independence for role checks without relying on UserProfile data, allowing for granular role management. QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters) Support: Path-Based Ownership: For /user_profiles/{userId} and /user_profiles/{userId}/visits/{visitId}, rules directly enforce ownership using the userId wildcard and the userId field in the document. This means list queries against these paths, when executed by a regular user, inherently conform to their ownership, preventing unauthorized data exposure and supporting QAPs. Structural Segregation: /visit_purposes is globally readable by authenticated users, making list queries efficient and secure for its specific access needs. Admin Access: Administrators can perform list operations on /user_profiles and use collection group queries on visits to retrieve aggregated data, with rules ensuring these broad access patterns are restricted to authenticated administrators. Regarding 'Daily Visitor Count': The application requirements include displaying a 'current number of visitors logged in for the day' and admin statistics based on daily counts. Due to the strict constraint that schema.$ref must point to one of the provided entities (UserProfile, VisitPurpose, Visit), a dedicated 'daily_statistics' collection (which would be ideal for storing this aggregate data) cannot be formally defined within this structure. This functionality would typically require a separate collection with an entityName like 'DailyStatistic'. As a workaround within the given constraints, this feature would need to be implemented either by performing expensive real-time aggregations via collection group queries on visits (potentially causing performance issues and rule complexity), or by using an external caching/aggregation service (e.g., Cloud Functions with Redis or another Firestore collection not explicitly linked to the provided entities).
